overal.goal: Every workspace manifest uses the `workspace:*` protocol, which npm does not support: `npm install` fails with EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL, so the install script's npm fallback (scripts/install-or-update-boof-runner.sh:187-194) and the README's `npm install` / `npm install -g .` claims are broken. Copy mode is broken a second way: bin/tsup.config.ts keeps hono, zod, gray-matter, chokidar and @hono/node-server external while the root package.json has no dependencies, so a global copy install dies with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Either require bun (and say so everywhere) or make npm work: replace `workspace:*` with `*`/file references npm accepts, and bundle the externals or list them as root dependencies. Acceptance: a CI job installs with npm on a clean checkout, runs the built CLI, and the README matches.
overal.stack: TypeScript monorepo (Node 22 / Bun), Hono server, React + Vite UI, vitest

rules.do: Read README.md and docs/boof-runner.md for the intended behaviour before changing code.
Write a failing test first, then make it pass; keep the change focused on this goal.
Run `npm run typecheck && npm test` and `npm run lint` before finishing.
Reproduce first with `npm install` in a clean clone; keep bun as the primary path.
rules.dont: Do not change public API or MCP shapes without updating docs/api.md and the OpenAPI document.
Do not commit secrets, data roots or build output.

versions.version: Identified during the 2026-10-27 review; not started.

Every workspace reference is "*" (npm and bun both link the workspace); the five CLI externals are root dependencies; package-lock.json is git-ignored and bun.lock regenerated; CI gains an npm-only job (npm install, build:server, --version, unknown command exits 1, npm install -g into a temp prefix); the install script's npm branch uses npm install and the docs say so. Finding: npm 10 symlinks a global directory install, so the copy-mode ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND did not reproduce; the manifests are fixed regardless.

tests.strategy: Unit tests with vitest for the changed module; an integration test through the Hono app or CLI where the behaviour is observable there.
